messages.text: Builds are slow again. Dependency install step is 8 minutes. Can we cache the layer?
We can. Lockfile hash as cache key—invalidate on package.json or lockfile change. I'll draft the strategy.
We use npm. Lockfile is committed. So key = hash(lockfile) and we store node_modules?
Store the archive of node_modules keyed by lockfile hash. Restore before install; run npm ci so we only fill gaps. Should cut install to under a minute when hit.
What about cache size? We have 40+ pipelines.
One cache per repo or per lockfile. Set a max number of cached entries and evict oldest. I can suggest a cap based on your storage budget.
We have 50GB for build caches. I'll implement the key strategy and add a job to prune old entries weekly.
Add metrics: hit rate and restore time. If hit rate drops, we'll know when to tune the key or increase the cap.
Will do. Fast and organized—exactly what the pipeline needs. Thanks.
Anytime. When you're ready, we can do the same for Docker layer caching.
